children: Overview
Hong Kong property developer's FY underlying profit and EPS declined year-on-year
Net profit rose due to smaller investment property revaluation loss
Revenue from property sales and rental activities both declined year-on-year
Outlook
Company says it will monitor macroeconomic and geopolitical developments amid ongoing uncertainties
Company expects government measures to support a stable property market and improved sentiment
Company sees positive trends in residential demand and leasing activity due to talent admission schemes and student quotas
Result Drivers
LOWER PROPERTY REVALUATION LOSS – Net profit rose as the non-cash revaluation loss on investment properties narrowed to HK$192 mln from HK$1.084 bln
RETAIL AND INDUSTRIAL PRESSURE – Net rental income fell 2.4% as challenging retail and industrial conditions reduced gross rental revenue, while new assets and tenancy mix lifted operating costs
HOTEL RECOVERY - Co said hotel revenue rose, supported by recovering tourist arrivals and stronger business and leisure demand

The stock recently traded at 20 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 23 three months ago
